title: Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary
main_claim: Every MMP (arbitrary negative extremal ray choices, divisorial/flip/mixed steps, no Q-factoriality or pseudo-effectivity) starting from a projective lc fourfold pair with rational boundary over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 exists at each step and terminates, ending at a nef lc pair or a Mori fibre space.

issues.description: The paper applies Birkar's Theorem 1.1 directly to the possibly non-Q-factorial lc pair (X/Z, B+A) and says it gives a good log minimal model. If the published statement needs Q-factorial dlt input, the standard fix is to pass to a dlt blowup and choose the general member G after the blowup. That reduction is not written out. The conclusion is not in doubt.
issues.evidence: Text: 'It does not assume Q-factoriality or ampleness of A. It gives a log minimal model or a Mori fibre space for (X/Z,B), and the adjoint on a nef log minimal model is semiample over Z.' The cited statement could not be checked offline, so this is taken on trust, as the earlier report for this paper on the board also noted.

issues.location: Sec. 4, Lemma 4.4 (finite monodromy via Quot parameter spaces)
issues.description: The argument is terse: it takes a very general fibre, uses components of the Quot parameter space that dominate the curve, and transports Chern classes along paths. I find it correct, but several routine points are only asserted: closedness and flatness of the invertible-quotient locus, and that the paths stay over the locus where the local system is defined.
issues.evidence: 'Choose a path in the parameter component from the original quotient point to a point on this cover. Flatness of the universal Chern class identifies the transported c_i with the class at that cover point.'

coverage:
I read all sections, 00 through 08. Each item below was checked step by step:
- Graph lemma: H>=0, its support is the full preimage of the bad locus, and dim W^- + dim W^+ >= 3.
- Cycle-rank localization (kernel = span of r-dimensional components) and the removal of divisor-losing and mixed steps.
- Terminal chain: the BCHM 1.4.3 extraction of I_0, effectivity of the decreased coefficients, the negativity comparison E>=0 with q_*E=0, the relative BCHM MMP over Z_i, the two-ends identification, and that no marked divisor is lost (crepancy against strict improvement).
- Echo classification: e(xi)=0 monomials of orders (j,1).
- Transverse-slice surface mld and ACC, which show varying labels have downstairs centres of codimension >= 3.
- Ceiling lemma: r_{V,h} <= m_h with residue degrees; the deficit r-1 from the ceiling inequality; b>1/2 forces a unique label of multiplicity 1, and the v_j pay the j>=2 defaults.
- Conductor estimate: normalization excision sequence, injectivity of H_4(F_Q) into H_4(F_{P_1}), weight -4 strictness, and the vanishing of H^BM_6(P\P_1).
- IC restriction purity: the support bound i+z<=2 from fibre stalk degrees, and the vanishing of degree-1 contributions from IC_X and from summands not supported in C.
- Cone of Q[4]->IC_Y: stalk bounds, H^{-2} = R^2 j_* Q on T°, and the surjection onto H^0(Q, T|_Q) giving b_T.
- Local valuations: H^2(F,O)=0 from rational singularities and formal functions; surjectivity of c_1; norms giving invariant classes over K_T; lifting with obstruction in H^2(J_n)=0, Grothendieck existence, and Artin approximation keeping the residue field; small Q-factorialization and degree independence via relative BPF descent; uniqueness of the étale restriction of valuations; and a=2, a_Theta<2.
- Flip cancellation: rho_*^- - rho_*^+ = e^- - e^+, using independence of contracted divisor classes.
- Unit drop: M = N(2-a^+) is an integer, and v is not in I_0, so it stays exceptional through the bridge.
- Dlt elementary steps, special termination reducing to klt, the vertical-ray lemma, nonempty dlt bridges, and smallness of the mixed-step continuation.
- Numerical field transfer, both for whole countable programs and for the finite continuation data.
Section 8 (consequences, which rely on companion papers) was only skimmed and is outside the main theorem.
sibling_notes: The board already had a rank-193 entry for this directory, from an earlier run, with the same verdict. I agree with it independently and updated the entry. Companion paper Oct-7 (generalized lc flips on compact Kähler 4-folds) uses the same branch-inequality architecture: Saito decomposition, weight-4 purity, finite monodromy. My check of Secs. 3–4 here supports the same core lemmas there. This paper does not depend on the companion papers for termination; only Sec. 8 uses OpenAI LogAbundance/Complements/Cartier.
